audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows contradicted their own whys in both layers: the chart gave Jax level 1 while the early text says 'you actually own level 1', gave Ornn levels 3 and 4-5 while whys[2] says 'Jax edges it' and whys[3] calls 4-5 'his cleanest window', and gave Jax level 6 while whys[4] opens 'Even at 6'.
audit.why: Packet chart is Ornn / Skill / Jax / Jax / Skill / Ornn / Ornn and the mirror (jax__ornn) flipped exactly these four rows as matched pairs.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3, 4 flipped as one atomic group across both layers; ratings set to 6,6,4,4,5,6,6.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere — Counter Strike was tracked with no idea how long it is down.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9s — a 17s window at rank 1 is an enormous punish gap, and it shrinks to 9s by the time he maxes it. Leap Strike is 8s, Empower 7s falling to 3s.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into phases[2].why, breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two absences. Volcanic Rupture grounds Leap Strike — his gap-closer and his exit — and Empower is an auto-attack reset, so the burst tell is the wind-up rather than the cast.
audit.why: Ornn Q carries grounding; Jax Q carries dash; Jax W carries autoReset. The auto reset is flagged in missingInteractions.
audit.corrected: Grounding written into report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns; the auto reset into dontsFull[0].d.

audit.why: The page already gets the important half right: Counter Strike dodges basic attacks, which is why the advice is to poke with Bellows Breath rather than auto into it. Riot's text says 'dodge all incoming attacks', i.e. basic attacks. The mirror reached the same conclusion. I made that explicit rather than changing it.
audit.corrected: Stated positively in dosFull[0].d, report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Jax must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Counter Strike (17s) dodges your autos and stuns — his window, so poke with Bellows Breath instead of trading.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Counter Strike's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: A second Counter Strike point wins his short trades, and a held E blanks your charge — bait the dodge before you commit anything.

edits.before: - Jax Counter Strike: matchup-defining — Dodges autos + stuns. Bait it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Jax Counter Strike: 17s at rank 1, 9s maxed — it dodges basic attacks, not Bellows Breath. - Leap Strike: 8s, and Volcanic Rupture grounds it. - Empower: 7s down to 3s, and it is an auto reset.

edits.before: Dodges autos + stuns. Bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 17s at rank 1. It dodges basic attacks — Bellows Breath still lands.

edits.before: Track Jax's Counter Strike: Dodges autos + stuns. Bait it. When it is down — W-E + R him.

edits.before: That is Jax's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.

notes: Name discrepancy worth resolving centrally: the packet lists Jax's R as 'Grandmaster-at-Arms' while the mirror audit corrected three fields on the Jax page to 'Grandmaster's Might'. This ornn entry never names his ultimate, so nothing was edited here, but the two sides of the site will disagree until one is picked. Also left standing as unverified: the repeated claim that Bellows Breath grants a shield and is unstoppable (spikes[0], early, wants.you[0]) — Riot's W text mentions neither, and the same fiction appears across this champion's other matchups. late references 'the lolalytics edge', which reads as leftover authoring scaffolding on a customer-facing page.
